alreadySet: •••• already set — leave blank to keep it

collection_cycle.label: Fast metrics
collection_cycle.description: Cache hit rate, connection count, worst table bloat, database size.

table_metrics_cycle.label: Per-table metrics
table_metrics_cycle.description: Per-table dead-tuple % and size, behind Trends' per-table picker.

plan_regression_cycle.label: Plan regression capture
plan_regression_cycle.description: Captures each tracked query's EXPLAIN plan shape, behind the Plan Regressions screen.

live_findings_cycle.label: Live findings history
live_findings_cycle.description: Persists Dashboard/Diagnose Now's live findings with first-seen tracking, and drives Actionable Alerting below.

retention_cycle.label: Metric retention
retention_cycle.description: Prunes metric samples older than 30 days.

deep_scan.label: Deep scan
deep_scan.description: Runs Index Advisor, Schema Lint, and Configuration Advisor against every active target and records what's still open, since when.

weekly_report.label: Weekly report
weekly_report.description: Builds each database's weekly health report (Monitor → Weekly Reports) and, if switched on below, posts its summary to the webhook.

scheduler.title: Scheduler
scheduler.description: How often each background job runs. Saving takes effect immediately — no backend restart needed.

ai.title: AI Query Analysis
ai.description: Configures the AI provider used by Query Intelligence's "Analyze with AI" button. Your query text and its EXPLAIN plan are sent to this provider — use the Anonymize option in the analysis window if that's a concern for a cloud provider.
ai.modelHint: Google retires model names fairly often — if analysis starts failing with a "model not found" error, check the current model list and update this field.

alerts.title: Actionable Alerting
alerts.description: Sends a webhook the moment a finding first opens at or above the chosen severity — driven by the "Live findings history" job above, so a problem is reported once when it starts, not every cycle it stays open. Paste a Slack, Discord, or Microsoft Teams webhook URL and the right payload format is detected automatically — no separate setting to pick.

kind.generic: Generic JSON (Mattermost and others compatible with Slack's format still work)

alerts.reportWebhook: Also post each weekly report's summary to this webhook (independent of the Enabled switch above)
alerts.testSent: Test alert sent — check your webhook's destination.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Read-only access for machines, each with its own token set in the server's .env (APP_MCP_TOKEN, APP_METRICS_TOKEN) — neither can use the rest of the API.
integrations.mcpText_one: Lets Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client ask "what's wrong with this database?" through {{count}} preset read-only tool. No tool runs SQL it's given, and query text goes out with literal values masked.
integrations.mcpText_other: Lets Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client ask "what's wrong with this database?" through {{count}} preset read-only tools. No tool runs SQL it's given, and query text goes out with literal values masked.
integrations.mcpOff: Set APP_MCP_TOKEN in .env and restart the backend to switch it on.
integrations.prometheusText: Collected metrics, open-finding counts and lock waits per database, for Grafana and Alertmanager. Also served at /metrics on the backend's own port.
integrations.metricsOff: Set APP_METRICS_TOKEN in .env and restart the backend to switch it on.
integrations.publicUrl: Set APP_PUBLIC_URL in .env to the address people open DbButler at: the weekly report's webhook message then links to the report, and the snippets above use it.
